summary: The paper automatically allocates scratchpad buffers for the data accessed by a block of computation and generates code that moves data between global and local memory. It also applies multi-level tiling, with tile sizes chosen by a cost model, to spread work across GPU multiprocessors and their inner SIMD units.
why_read: It shows how a compiler can manage explicitly managed memories and map polyhedral loop nests onto a two-level parallel machine, a useful precursor for polyhedral code generation on distributed memory.
main_contribution: An automatic framework for scratchpad buffer allocation and data-movement code generation, combined with multi-level tiling and a tile-size search for a GPU.
main_limitation: Copy-in and copy-out sets are not yet reduced using dependence information, and the evaluation covers two kernels on one GPU.
evaluation_method: Measured execution time on a GeForce 8800 GTX against GPU-only global memory and a CPU
states_relationship_to: Bondhugula et al. 2007 affine transformation framework [7]
